BMW’s M3 EV Hits the Road Looking Like a Toned-Down M Concept Neue Klasse
17 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
BMW has several new models in the making, and one of them is the range-topping version of the latest i3 Sedan, namely the M3 Electric .
This is what it should be called, as the Munich-based auto marque reportedly went for this name rather than christen it the i3 M or the iM3 because the automaker wanted enthusiasts to know that this is a real M car. Therefore, it has some big shoes to fill, because the M3 has always been a great driver’s car, regardless of the generation, so petrolheads have huge expectations when it comes to the driving part of the first-ever M3 Electric.
Despite the fact that we have encountered various prototypes of the upcoming BMW M3 Electric on several occasions, and that the model has also been teased, and has also fallen into the hands of the rendering crowd, its specifications remain a well-guarded secret. Nevertheless, reports indicate that it will feature a quad-motor setup with all-wheel drive, and from here on, you’ll get contradicting data if you try to look up the output.
That’s because while some believe that this model might offer in the region of 700 horsepower, others claim that around 800 horsepower is a more realistic figure. And there are also those who would argue that a four-digit output could also be a thing. After all, the platform, which is the Neue Klasse NAx, definitely supports this much power. However, we really would not hold our breath for roughly 1,000 horsepower or so.
Photo: SH Proshots Actually, not at first, anyway, because further down the line, BMW’s M Division could launch a CS version of the M3 Electric in order to make it more appealing, and it is this one that might get close or perhaps enter the four-digit realm. That’s my opinion, and you should take it with a pinch of salt. Realistically speaking, some 800 horsepower seems possible After all, it will take a swing at the Mercedes-AMG C-Class Electric, which is said to have a tri-motor setup with approximately 800 horsepower.
Our spies have read some recent reports that spoke about an estimated 850 horsepower, so they believe that this will be the output of the BMW M3 Electric, which is understood to tip the scales at roughly 2.3 metric tons, or over 5,000 pounds. The battery pack should have a capacity of around 100 kWh, enabling a rumored 650 km (400+ miles) or so range on the WLTP cycle, and supposedly charging at up to 420 kW. Adding up to 350 km (217 miles) of range might take around 10 minutes or so.
Keep in mind that the outputs mentioned in the above paragraphs are in metric horsepower, as the companies are European, they are testing these models on the other side of the Atlantic Ocean. However, as you already know, they will touch down in the United States of America . When will that happen? Probably sometime next year when it comes to both of them. Or at least that is when they are expected to premiere.
In the meantime, we will keep encountering prototypes in the open, and the pixel-altering crowd will keep having its way with them, though the BMW M3 Electric is definitely getting a lot more attention than its rival from the Affalterbach brand. And this story is also about it, as the scoops shared in the gallery just ended up in our inboxes, with our spy photographer managing to immortalize the prototype in question as it was being driven on public roads.
Photo: SH Proshots Due to the quite trippy camouflage, it stood out immediately, and we can clearly see that it looks pretty much like a toned down version of the BMW M Concept Neue Klasse unveiled earlier this year. And it’s not exactly a surprise, because we expected that. We can see a similar take when it comes to the front and rear bumpers, as well as the front hood, and other parts of the exterior.
The BMW M3 Electric appears to have wider tracks compared to the lesser i3 Sedan, on which it builds, and we expect a few changes on the inside too. There, the front seats should offer more lateral support, likely featuring integrated headrests. Exclusive trim and upholstery, as well as some carbon fiber inserts, should be part of the M makeover of the i3 Sedan, alongside dedicated load screens and submenus for the displays, including the Panoramic iDrive that stretches at the bottom of the windshield.
We still have plenty of things to find out about the first-ever BMW M3 Electric , and we expect the upcoming scooped testers to gradually start losing camouflage as the testing and fine-tuning phase of this model advances. As previously mentioned, the unveiling might take place next year, and it should hit our shores either for the 2027 or maybe the 2028 model year. We lean on the latter rather than the former.
